general_notes: All work shall comply with the 2021 IRC as adopted and amended by the City of Centennial (CMC Ch. 18) and the 2023 NEC. The stamped structural drawings govern.
Design loads: deck 40 psf live + 10 psf dead; ground snow 30 psf (roofs 30 psf non-reducible); wind 115 mph Vult, Risk Cat. II; SDC B; frost depth 36 in.; soil 1,500 psf presumptive.
Framing lumber No. 2 or better, preservative-treated per AWPA U1 (ground-contact where within 6" of grade) or approved naturally durable; field cuts treated per AWPA M4 (IRC R507.2.1, R317).
Fasteners and connectors hot-dip galvanized or stainless per IRC Table R507.2.3; connectors per the manufacturer for the treatment used.

Ledgers 2x8 min. PT into the house rim: 1/2" HDG lags at 18" o.c. staggered (joist span 10' or less) or LedgerLOK per DrJ TER 1203-03; flashed per IRC R507.2.4 / R703.4. No ledger on brick veneer or the chimney: free-standing beam on posts there.
Lateral load connection at each deck level: (4) hold-down devices of 750 lb min. per IRC Fig. R507.9.2(2).

Footings: 24" x 42" concrete caissons (30" under the upper level with the roof) below finished grade (frost depth 36"), (4) #4 + #3 ties, sized by the engineer (1,500 psf presumptive). The ones under the upper level are drilled through saw-cut openings 6" wider than the hole in the patio slab with a 1/2" isolation joint and poured flush; the bed caissons stand 7" above finished grade. 8x8 DF rough columns on Simpson ABU88RZ set once the caisson has cured, on (2) 5/8" Titen HD screw anchors drilled into it (never wet-set). PE observation of the holes and rebar before each pour (R109.1.1). Call 811 before drilling.

Posts 8x8 DF-L, 14'-0" max. beam to footing (IRC Table R507.4); beams 6x10 DF per the engineer; joists 2x10 SYP at 12" o.c. (IRC Table R507.6); hangers and post / beam connectors sized to the members.

Guards 36" min. at every open side more than 30" above the floor or grade below, including the 37" step between the levels; openings under 4"; 200 lb top load. TimberTech Impression Rail Express per ICC-ES ESR-4217, posts 91-5/16" o.c. max.

Stairs: risers 7-3/4" max. (3/8" max. variation), treads 10" min. (nosing 3/4"-1-1/4" where under 11"), width 36" min.; graspable handrail 34"-38" on one side of every flight of 4 or more risers; guards on open sides; landings 36" min. in the direction of travel.

A light source at the top landing of each exterior stair (IRC R303.8). A receptacle accessible from each deck level (NEC 210.52(E)(3)), GFCI, weather-resistant, in-use cover. Low-voltage lighting Class 2, listed (NEC 411).
Decking TimberTech Vintage (Intertek CCRR-0101) on joists at 12" o.c.; stair treads and stringer spacing per the manufacturer.

Inspections: footings (the caisson holes + rebar before each pour, PE observation per R109.1.1) - framing (before decking) - electrical - final. Keep a 36" x 36" path from any egress window under the deck (IRC R310.2.4).

items: Your purchase. The house is listed for sale, and the county record shows it held by the seller's trust. The HOA request and the other owner signatures go in your name, so they follow your closing. Please tell us your closing date.

HOA approval. The Tiffany HOA approves decks and patio covers in writing before work starts. The request goes in at least 3 weeks ahead, with the drawings and samples of the English Walnut board, the black rail and the black roof. The HOA asks owners to talk with the neighbors before they apply.

How the deck meets the house. The house has brick veneer, and behind the main sections the main floor may cantilever 2' past the walk-out wall. Nothing is fastened to brick. The engineer decides whether the deck is fastened to the house's wood band there or stands on its own beams and columns.
Engineering. A Colorado structural engineer stamps the drawings before we order: the 6x10 beams and the roof's loads call for it.
Measurements. The heights in this proposal come from photos. The deck heights, the arm's length and the eave over the upper level are taped on site before the drawings are final.

Outlet and stair light. Each level needs an outdoor outlet within reach, and each stair needs a light at its top: Option 1's riser lights light the stairs. We check what is there now; adding an outlet is work for a licensed electrician.
